_about: The first scheme with a fight in it. Seven thousand creature stat blocks ship and
no quest had ever put one in front of the player: every shipped scheme resolves
in conversation, travel or an item changing hands.
It is the only user of two criteria the grammar has always had — `arrived($slot)`,
which fires on getting somewhere rather than on being there, and
`event:fight_ended`, which is how a scheme learns the encounter closed without
asking who won. What it reads instead is who is still alive, because a fight the
player ran away from also ends.

The threat is not a slot. `bring_in` takes role words and asks the codex for
something near the party's level, so this is a bandit at first level, a poacher
around sixth and a bandit lord in the teens without authoring any of them.
It is men and not a beast because the codex is a codex of people: asking it for
'beast' returns a troglodyte beast-speaker, and 'wolf' a ghost wolf warrior, both
matched on the word in a humanoid's name. That turned out to be the better story —
tracks wrong for a wolf because nothing with paws made them.
item slot resolves to an ingredient from the forage catalogue whatever the slot is
called, so the tell came out as 'there is Chasmyre Leaf on the ground here, and the
spacing is wrong for a wolf'. Found by opening the scheme against both shipped
worlds rather than by the lint, which has no opinion about whether a sentence means
anything.

schemes.title: What takes the herds
schemes.about: Something out past the edge is taking animals, and the tracks are wrong for a wolf.

cards.title: Find what is taking $elder's animals
objectives: Deal with whatever is doing it
cards.reward: the pick of what is left of the herd, and $elder's word at $market

cards.title: What the tracks actually say
facts: It is not a wolf and $elder half knows it: the spacing is wrong, and so is the depth.
They are men, working the same ground long enough to have a camp out at $wild, and they drive the animals off rather than bring them down.

grants_on_open.say: $elder said wolf twice, and did not look at you either time

also.text: The tracks at $wild are not a wolf's, whatever $elder wanted them to be.

tell.perceptible: There are tracks on the ground here at $wild, and the spacing is wrong for a wolf.
They have been camped here, and they are between you and the way back.

also.says: $elder has lost more animals out past $wild and is asking after anyone who went to look.

tell.silent: They are still out at $wild, and $elder is telling it at $market as a wolf again.
